why:
Real incident: Alex Eala Fan Club and Fearless Female Fighters both dropped to 0 posts for multiple consecutive days (p78 last real post Sep28 05:04 UTC, p55 last real post Sep25 05:05 UTC, over 3 and 4+ days silent respectively at the time of this fix). MMA Archives (p72) added 2026-09-30: same shape, 0.2 posts/day average over the prior 5 days -- its real candidate pool replays to 43 of 53 fresh candidates NO_NAMED_ENTITY (correct: real news about OTHER, unregistered UFC fighters) and its evergreen tier contributes almost nothing, because its 4 registered subjects (Anderson Silva, Georges St-Pierre, Ronda Rousey, Khabib Nurmagomedov) are retired-or-near-retired legends whose real WP-tagged coverage (864/764/1712/5230 articles respectively -- large, real archives) skews much older than 21 days: measured 2/2/5/3 articles per legend in the last 21 days vs 7/5/7/20 in 45 days. Three separate, evidenced supply bugs, not a relevance-gate problem -- checking with the pipeline's own compiled deterministic gates confirms the rejections are almost entirely correct NO_NAMED_ENTITY (real ATP/men's-UFC news that genuinely doesn't name any of these pages' registered subjects).

1) Alex Eala's registered entity name ('Alex Eala') resolves to WordPress tag id 83088 (17 articles total, 4 in the last 21 days) via queryArticlesByEntity -- but the real, much bigger tag ES actually uses for her is 'Alexandra Eala' (id 36420, 109 articles total, 9 in the last 21 days, 23 in 45 days). Same class of bug as the Dale Earnhardt Sr. tag rename (threads#47's predecessor patch): a page's registered slot NAME feeds the WP tag lookup directly (sourceFromEsArticles/sourceFromEsEvergreenArticles/resolveExternalLink all call queryArticlesByEntity(entity.name, ...)), and WP's tag search prefers an exact match over the higher-count real tag, so 'Alex Eala' the query silently locks onto the wrong, 6x-smaller tag. Renamed to 'Alexandra Eala' to match the real tag; keywords already include 'eala' (a substring of 'Alexandra Eala' too), so text-matching against real headlines is unaffected.

2) Both pages are individual-athlete/small-roster pages whose registered subjects' news is inherently bursty (a fighter/player between camps/tournaments can go weeks without coverage), not daily -- the fleet-wide 21-day evergreen freshness cutoff (built for steady-volume TEAM pages, to stop months-old news being pushed as current) means the entire evergreen tier goes silently empty between news cycles. Verified directly against the real WP tag counts: Eala's real tag has 9 articles in the last 21 days vs 23 in 45 days; the 7 women on Fearless Female Fighters combine for ~7 articles in 21 days vs ~25 in 45 days. Set evergreen_max_age_days=45 on both (opt-in, threads#48; no other page is affected).

Honest expectation, not a guarantee: this raises Alex Eala's realistic evergreen supply roughly 3-6x (4 -> 11-15 candidates in the replay, depending on whether the tag fix alone or combined with the window is measured) and Fearless Female Fighters' roughly 4x (4 -> 15) -- Eala should now sustain 3+/day most days. Fearless Female Fighters' 7 registered women combine for genuinely thin news even at 45 days (several -- Julianna Pena, Amanda Nunes -- had 0-1 articles in 60 days, suggesting they may not be the most currently-active roster for this page); this fix will meaningfully help but may not hit 3/day on a day when none of the 7 have real news, without either loosening a relevance gate (not done here) or refreshing the roster to currently-more-active fighters (a bigger, separate decision, flagged to the operator, not done here).
